turns.prompt_text: One of my friends Devin likes to use Microsoft Excel. What's a good book I could give him to improve his skills? It could also be an online course.
turns.response_html:
Since Devin already likes using Excel, he likely has the basics down and might appreciate resources that help him master advanced features or specialized data analysis. Here are the best book and course options for improving his skills.

Top Book Recommendations

For a gift, books that serve as a comprehensive reference or a deep dive into specific professional skills are usually best.

The "Gold Standard" Reference If you want to give him the ultimate resource that covers almost everything, the Microsoft Excel 365 Bible is the best choice. It is massive and detailed, serving as a long-term reference guide for everything from basic formulas to advanced VBA scripting. It’s perfect for someone who wants to know "how to do anything" in Excel.

Microsoft Excel 365 Bible

For the Aspiring Data Analyst If Devin uses Excel primarily for work, business, or analyzing data, Microsoft Excel Data Analysis and Business Modeling is a fantastic choice. It focuses less on "where the buttons are" and more on how to use Excel to solve real-world business problems, build models, and make decisions. It is written by Wayne Winston, a highly respected educator in the field.

Microsoft Excel Data Analysis and Business Modeling (Office 2021 and Microsoft 365)

Other Excellent Book Options:

  • Excel All-in-One For Dummies: A great, less intimidating alternative to the "Bible" if he prefers a friendlier tone. It breaks learning down into manageable "mini-books" on topics like formatting, formulas, and data analysis.
  • 101 Most Popular Excel Formulas: This is a smaller, more focused book that is perfect if he specifically wants to master formulas and functions without wading through pages of general interface instructions.

Top Online Course Recommendations

If he prefers interactive learning, these are the top-rated online programs for 2024-2025:

  • Coursera - "Excel Skills for Business" (Macquarie University): This is widely considered one of the best comprehensive online courses. It is structured like a university curriculum and covers everything from "Essentials" to "Advanced" skills. It’s excellent if he wants a structured path with quizzes and certificates.
  • Udemy - "Microsoft Excel - Excel from Beginner to Advanced" (Kyle Pew): This is a very popular, affordable "buy once, keep forever" video course. It’s less academic than Coursera and great for self-paced learning.
  • Udemy - Leila Gharani's Courses: If he is already advanced, look for courses by Leila Gharani. She specializes in advanced visualization, dashboards, and VBA (programming in Excel), which are great for "power users."

Summary: Which one to pick?

  • Choose the Microsoft Excel 365 Bible if you want to give him a physical reference book he can keep on his desk for years.
  • Choose Data Analysis and Business Modeling if he is interested in the math/business side of Excel rather than just learning the software features.
  • Choose an Online Course (like Coursera) if he prefers watching videos and doing interactive practice exercises over reading.

If you know which version of Excel he uses (e.g., Excel for Mac, Office 365, or an older version like 2019), I can double-check that these books are fully compatible for you.
